extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, registered patent agents, professional patent illustrators, and IP practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Produce and evaluate patent drawings that meet USPTO/MPEP formal requirements for utility and design patent applications (including filing, correction, and prosecution considerations). Focuses on formatting, labeling, view requirements, and common rejection avoidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings required where necessary (MPEP § 608.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter to be patented (MPEP § 608.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether a drawing is necessary to understand the claimed invention; drawings often determine whether claims are fully supported under 35 U.S.C. § 112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black ink only (color only by petition and explanation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be in black ink only (except color drawings with petition and explanation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default requirement is black ink/lines. Color drawings are permitted only if a petition and convincing explanation are submitted and granted — treat color as exceptional, not standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR 1.84 formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes formal formatting rules (margins, figure labels, paper size, reproducibility). Non-compliance with 1.84 will trigger formal objections during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducible at 2/3 scale without loss of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be reproducible at 2/3 scale without loss of detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure line weights, text, and fine details remain clear when reduced to two-thirds size; avoid overly fine hatchings or tiny reference numerals that become illegible when scaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include reference numerals, lead lines, and identifiers; use Arabic numerals and sequential numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Include reference numerals, lead lines, and identifiers. Use Arabic numerals to label elements (e.g., 100, 102, 104). Figures must be numbered sequentially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every labeled element in the specification appears in the drawings and vice versa. Use a consistent, sequential numbering scheme (Fig. 1, Fig. 2, …) and Arabic numerals for elements to avoid examiner objections for missing or inconsistent reference numerals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure labeling convention (e.g., 'Fig. 1')
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit Figures labeled as 'Fig. 1', 'Fig. 2', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard figure-label formatting. Improper or missing figure labels can lead to formal objections under 37 CFR 1.84.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper type, size, and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be on 21.6 x 27.9 cm (8.5 x 11 inch) white, non-glossy, durable paper and maintain 1-inch margins on all sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified paper and margin dimensions exactly. Deviations cause formal objections; durable, non-glossy stock and correct margins help with scanning and reproduction quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid black lines; no color/grayscale/shading unless required
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain solid black lines; no color, grayscale, or shading (unless required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid grayscale fills or photographic-style shadings unless a color or special shading is justified and permitted. For utility drawings, prefer crisp solid black line art; for design patents certain surface shading is permitted (see design shading rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple views for utility patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility patent illustrations should include multiple views: perspective, top, side, cross-sectional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all views necessary to show claimed features clearly. Cross-sectional views must be labeled and drawn to show internal structure; include perspective and orthogonal views as needed for full understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of broken lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Use broken lines only to show unclaimed environment or alternate positions (utility); in design patents use broken lines to disclaim unclaimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broken lines should not be used to depict claimed features. For design applications, use broken/dashed lines to show contextual or non-claimed elements; misuse can lead to confusion and rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent drawings are the entire disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike utility applications, design patent drawings are the entire disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because drawings constitute the whole of the disclosure for design patents, they must completely and clearly show the claimed visual appearance — omissions or ambiguities cannot be corrected by a written description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent view requirements (minimum seven views)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design drawings must include at least 7 views: front, back, top, bottom, left, right, and perspective (MPEP § 1503.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the full set of required views; missing views can be fatal to design prosecution. Consider additional detailed views or sectional views if necessary to show contour or ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface shading for design patents to show contour
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate surface shading to show contour in design patent drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply shading techniques consistently and conservatively to indicate three-dimensional shape; improper or inconsistent shading can mislead the scope of the claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistencies between views (design patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inconsistencies between views; a minor inconsistency (e.g., asymmetry in perspective vs. side view) can result in 35 U.S.C. § 112 rejections or a lack of enablement rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check all views for symmetry, proportionality, and consistent element placement. Use CAD/3D renders as references to ensure consistency across views and prevent enablement or written-description disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure drawings show every feature described in the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility patents, illustrations must show every feature described in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map claim language to drawing elements during drafting to ensure each claimed limitation is depicted; failures lead to § 112 support issues and examiner objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement and correction procedures for drawings (MPEP § 608.02(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers amendments to drawings and how to submit corrected figures via replacement sheets or marked‑up drawings (MPEP § 608.02(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When correcting drawings after filing, follow USPTO rules for replacement sheets and clearly identify changes. Improper amendment procedures can be rejected or treated as new matter if not handled correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common quality pitfalls: missing reference numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing Reference Numerals: Ensure every labeled element in the written specification appears in the drawings and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run cross-checks between spec and figures to ensure all reference numerals are present and consistently used; missing numerals commonly trigger Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common quality pitfalls: poor line quality and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor Line Quality: USPTO mandates clear, dark, solid lines; avoid fuzzy or pixelated output from low-res scans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-resolution vector artwork or high-DPI scans. Avoid thin hairlines and anti-aliased raster output that degrades when printed or reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common quality pitfalls: improper formatting (margins, labels, paper size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Compliance with 37 CFR 1.84 Formatting: Improper margins, figure labels, or paper size will trigger formal objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate each figure against 1.84 requirements before filing. Use templates or professional illustrators familiar with USPTO formatting to avoid formal objections that delay prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use professional tools and references to prevent errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use professional CAD software and 3D render references to prevent errors and inconsistencies between views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ CAD and controlled-render workflows for complex shapes to ensure reproducibility, accurate proportions, and consistency across multiple views; this helps prevent design inconsistencies and examiner rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure drawings are properly identified and filed with the application (MPEP § 601.01(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure drawings are properly identified and filed with the application (MPEP § 601.01(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that drawings are included in the application parts and identified per MPEP guidance at filing to avoid procedural deficiencies that could delay examination.
